answer: A work-and-stake registry resists sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond and a history of costly computation before voting or earning. Like light through a prism, one operator splitting into many identities pays rising cost: each lotus account must lock funds and finish time-bound tasks that cannot be cheaply parallelized, while peers audit and slash bonds for duplicates. An attacker seeking a thousand fake voices must pay a thousand bonds and workloads, so the nectar of influence costs more than it yields, while honest newcomers join with one modest stake.
